# C-03: deterministic topology and metrics

## 2 October: advanced Four Locks mathematical generation published

This entry supersedes the earlier T4/5 mathematical-generator pending statements below. C-03 remains IN_PROGRESS: runtime still exposes only the certified T1 reference, with no advanced mission bank or tactical certification.

Changed files in this batch: `expeditions/v2/generation/advanced-sudoku.js`, `advanced-sudoku.test.js`, `four-locks.js`, `four-locks.test.js`, `runtime-generation.test.js`, `scripts/dev/prove-four-locks-advanced.mjs`, `docs/expeditions/v2/fixtures/four-locks-advanced-generation.json` and this report. C-02 records the supporting puzzle changes. No Claude-owned engine, planner, App or shared build output was edited.

T4 generation now seeds canonical symbol/band/row/stack/column transformations, removes shuffled printed cells from a complete grid and changes shuffled cages while proving exhaustive uniqueness after every accepted change. Targets are exactly 1–2 givens and 5–7 connected cages. Every accepted trace completes with both an actual naked-pair elimination and cage-to-group intersection. T5 uses exactly 0–2 givens and 5–8 connected cages, a real pair elimination and a proved causal dependency between different cage reductions. The trace records candidate domains, local cage completions, removed candidates and counterfactual completions showing the downstream deduction depended on the earlier restriction. Optional contradiction uses one assumption per branch and at most one accepted contradiction in the complete human trace; no nested assumptions or exhaustive solver are used for that deduction. Independent exhaustive enumeration remains a separate uniqueness check.

Executable checks:

```text
node --test --test-reporter=dot expeditions/v2/generation/advanced-sudoku.test.js expeditions/v2/generation/four-locks.test.js expeditions/v2/generation/runtime-generation.test.js expeditions/v2/puzzles/puzzles.test.js
node scripts/dev/prove-four-locks-advanced.mjs
```

Outcome: 35/35 targeted tests pass. The proof runner publishes complete traces for six T4 successes at seeds 0, 1, 29, 53, 100 and 4294967295, and four T5 successes at seeds 0, 29, 53 and 100. T5 seeds 1 and 4294967295 remain honest `unknown` after 256 attempts. The six pinned T1–3 generation hashes remain unchanged. Production-reducer replay of both existing certified T1 routes still wins in the runtime tests. T4/5 candidates remain uncertified, with null certificate IDs, unchanged output costs, output budget 8, charge/integrity rules, enemy wake phase and deadline. Runtime availability explicitly rejects both tiers. No full rebuild or shared output mutation was performed.

Evidence: `docs/expeditions/v2/fixtures/four-locks-advanced-generation.json`. It records exact givens/cages, construction transformations and accepted uniqueness checks, full human traces, rejections and the optional seed29 contradiction branch. No screenshot was produced for this mathematical batch.

Ready dependency: advanced Four Locks puzzle candidates and independently checked mathematical evidence are available to C-08A/Claude's production-reducer tactical planner. They are not permission to expose advanced missions. Unresolved: the three verified starting patterns do not establish required bank diversity; T4/5 mission playability remains unproved; actual private App integration and QA-01 remain pending. No other-family packet has been expanded.

2 October advanced Four Locks batch claims: `expeditions/v2/generation/advanced-sudoku.js`, `advanced-sudoku.test.js`, `scripts/dev/prove-four-locks-advanced.mjs`, `docs/expeditions/v2/fixtures/four-locks-advanced-generation.json`, plus existing owned `four-locks.js`/tests. Use the three independently verified mathematical patterns as construction starting points, then seed canonical transformations and constraint changes. Every accepted final puzzle must independently solve uniquely and satisfy the exact tier targets with a full human trace. Starting patterns are not tactical certificates or a diversity bank. Pin all sampled T1–3 hashes before editing; runtime availability stays T1 only.

Owner: Codex. Baseline 1.0, coordination 1.1. State: CLAIMED.
